meta.decision_rationale: Brand DNA synthesizes the library's essential identity from scenarios and competitive position, guiding all downstream governance and collection decisions.
evidence_refs: Phase 1 scenarios (esp. Civic Hub preferred, Politicized feared)
Community survey data on values (equity, accessibility, intellectual freedom)
tradeoffs: Explicit value statements may alienate some stakeholders
Committing to values in writing creates accountability

radical_values.tested_in: A 2025 challenge to remove several titles from the shelves after political pressure.
radical_values.cost_paid: Lost a conditional grant tied to removing the contested titles.

radical_values.tested_in: Debate over introducing paid premium services to close a budget gap.
radical_values.cost_paid: Forwent recurring premium-subscription revenue to keep all services free.

radical_values.tested_in: Pressure to let a single donor dictate collection priorities.
radical_values.cost_paid: Declined a major earmarked donation to preserve community governance.

accepted_biases: Preference for local and independent authors over bestseller optimization
Bias toward physical and hybrid gathering over purely digital delivery
brand_dna.moral_entity: A community-accountable steward of knowledge that treats access to information as a public good rather than a product.
refusal_zones: Algorithmic collection decisions driven by engagement metrics
Censorship of lawful materials under political or commercial pressure

acceptable: Slower decisions in exchange for transparent community deliberation
Narrower bestseller selection in exchange for diverse, curated breadth
unacceptable: Trading equity of access for short-term revenue
